questions.question: You hear a vaccine claim you are unsure about. What should you do?

answers.text: Verify it with a reliable source or healthcare professional.
Believe it if many people agree with it.
Trust it if another parent experienced it.
Share it and see what others think.

questions.explanation: Reliable sources and healthcare professionals can help confirm if a claim is true.

questions.question: Why should vaccine information be verified?

answers.text: False information can affect health decisions.
Different parents may have different opinions.
Online information is always unreliable.
Only doctors need to understand vaccine information.

questions.explanation: Checking information helps you avoid myths and make informed health decisions.

questions.question: Who should you ask about your child's vaccines?

answers.text: A qualified healthcare professional.
Another parent with a similar experience.
A trusted family member.
An online parenting group.

questions.explanation: Healthcare professionals can provide reliable guidance about vaccines.

questions.question: You find two conflicting vaccine claims. What should you do?

answers.text: Check reliable sources and ask a healthcare professional.
Choose the claim with more likes.
Choose the one your friends believe.
Accept both claims as equally true.

questions.explanation: Reliable sources can help you determine which information is accurate.

questions.question: Why shouldn't you rely only on other parents' experiences?

answers.text: Personal experiences may not apply to every child.
Parents cannot have opinions about vaccines.
Only online information can be trusted.
Every child's experience with vaccines is identical.

questions.explanation: Personal experiences can differ, so health concerns should be checked with a professional.
